quote.text: When you wake up in the morning, tell yourself: the people I deal with today will be meddling, ungrateful, arrogant, dishonest, jealous and surly. They are like this because they can't tell good from evil. But I have seen the beauty of good, and the ugliness of evil, and have recognized that the wrongdoer has a nature related to my own - not of the same blood and birth, but the same mind, and possessing a share of the divine. And so none of them can hurt me. No one can implicate me in ugliness. Nor can I feel angry at my relative, or hate him. We were born to work together like feet, hands and eyes, like the two rows of teeth, upper and lower. To obstruct each other is unnatural. To feel anger at someone, to turn your back on him: these are unnatural.
quote.author: Marcus Aurelius
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Recognize that your children, like all people, will sometimes act out of ignorance rather than malice; this understanding helps you nurture compassion instead of reacting in anger.
    • Just as I remind myself daily to choose virtue over frustration, guide your children by exemplifying patience and unconditional support, knowing that mutual respect breeds growth.
  • Leadership
    • Embrace the reality that those you lead may display shortcomings—arrogance, ungratefulness, or dishonesty—as part of their human nature; meet them with equanimity rather than retaliation.
    • Lead by fostering an environment where every individual is seen as part of a larger, interconnected whole, encouraging cooperation and understanding rather than hostility.
  • Product Management
    • In the realm of product management, expect diverse opinions and occasional discord; understand that such diversity stems from varying levels of experience and perspectives, much like the natural differences between individuals.
    • Channel your inner calm to build a cohesive team where disagreements become opportunities for creative problem-solving, keeping the focus on collective improvement rather than individual flaws.
